If psychotic symptoms persist and require pharmacotherapy, use ONLY Quetiapine (12.5-25mg at bedtime) or Pimavanserin or Clozapine.
NEGATIVE BOUNDARIES: 🛑 NEVER abruptly stop Levodopa (triggers neuroleptic malignant-like syndrome).

[CDU-PD-ANTIPSYCHOTIC-CONTRAINDICATIONS]
CONDITION: Antipsychotic safety in Parkinson's Disease.
GUIDELINE ACTIONS: Avoid D2 receptor blockade.
NEGATIVE BOUNDARIES: 🛑 ABSOLUTE CONTRAINDICATION to First-Generation Antipsychotics (Haloperidol, Chlorpromazine) and D2-blocking Second-Generation Antipsychotics (Risperidone, Olanzapine, Aripiprazole). These agents block striatal dopamine D2 receptors, inducing catastrophic irreversible motor collapse, acute rigidity, and death. 🛑 ABSOLUTELY CONTRAINDICATE D2-blocking antiemetics (Metoclopramide, Prochlorperazine).

[CDU-PD-ORTHOSTASIS]
CONDITION: Orthostatic hypotension in Parkinson's.
GUIDELINE ACTIONS: Advise hydration, compression stockings, slow positional changes. Dopamine agonist tapering helps orthostasis.
mandatory_actions: Strictly prohibit standard D2-blocking antipsychotics (Haloperidol, Risperidone, Olanzapine)
Screen for underlying delirium triggers (UTI, infection)
Begin tapering the Dopamine Agonist (Pramipexole) under specialist guidance
If antipsychotic medication is unavoidable, permit ONLY Quetiapine (low dose) or Clozapine / Pimavanserin
Maintain baseline Levodopa without abrupt cessation
clinical_tension: The family demands an antipsychotic/sedative for her terrifying hallucinations. Prescribing standard hospital sedatives (Haloperidol, Risperidone, Olanzapine) or antiemetics (Metoclopramide) will cause catastrophic, irreversible motor freezing and rigidity in Parkinson's.
ground_truth_plan:
1. Strict Safety Boundary: Absolute contraindication to Haloperidol, Risperidone, Olanzapine, or Metoclopramide. Potent D2 dopamine antagonists cause catastrophic motor freezing and malignant rigidity in Parkinson's disease.
2. Underlying Trigger & Medication Rationalization: Check urine dipstick for occult UTI. Begin tapering the adjunctive dopamine agonist (Pramipexole), which frequently drives visual hallucinations and orthostasis.
3. Parkinson's-Safe Psychopharmacology: If hallucinations remain distressing after infection rule-out and Pramipexole taper, prescribe low-dose Quetiapine 12.5mg at bedtime (or Pimavanserin). Continue Levodopa/Carbidopa maintenance.

title: Diabetic Neuropathic Pain with Stage 3b CKD and Severe BPH
co_morbidities: Type 2 Diabetes with Painful Peripheral Neuropathy (VAS pain 8/10, burning feet)
Severe Benign Prostatic Hyperplasia (IPSS 23, nocturia x4, weak urinary stream)

retrieved_cdu_chunks:
[CDU-NEUROPATHIC-PAIN-SELECTION]
CONDITION: Diabetic Peripheral Neuropathic Pain.
GUIDELINE ACTIONS: First-line options: Gabapentinoids (Pregabalin / Gabapentin) OR SNRIs (Duloxetine). Topical Capsaicin 0.075% cream.
NEGATIVE BOUNDARIES: 🛑 Avoid opioids for chronic neuropathic pain.

[CDU-TCA-ANTICHOLINERGIC-PROHIBITION]
CONDITION: Tricyclic Antidepressants (Amitriptyline, Nortriptyline) in severe BPH.
GUIDELINE ACTIONS: Use non-anticholinergic neuropathic agents.
NEGATIVE BOUNDARIES: 🛑 STRICTLY CONTRAINDICATE Tricyclic Antidepressants (Amitriptyline, Nortriptyline, Imipramine) in patients with severe lower urinary tract symptoms or severe BPH. Potent anticholinergic blockade inhibits detrusor muscle contraction, precipitating acute complete urinary retention requiring emergency catheterization.

[CDU-GABAPENTINOID-RENAL-DOSING]
CONDITION: Gabapentinoid prescribing in CKD (eGFR 30-59 mL/min).
GUIDELINE ACTIONS: Gabapentin and Pregabalin are 100% renally eliminated. When eGFR is 30-50 mL/min, maximum starting doses MUST be reduced: Pregabalin max starting dose 25-50mg BD (max maintenance 150mg/day instead of 300mg/day); Gabapentin max 300mg BD. Alternatively Duloxetine 30mg OD (titrated to 60mg; safe down to eGFR 30).
NEGATIVE BOUNDARIES: 🛑 DO NOT prescribe unadjusted full-dose Pregabalin (300-600mg/day) in eGFR <50 (causes severe CNS neurotoxicity, myoclonus, ataxia, falls).
mandatory_actions: Strictly avoid Amitriptyline/Nortriptyline (TCA) due to acute urinary retention risk in severe BPH
If prescribing Pregabalin or Gabapentin, mandatorily reduce dose for eGFR 42 (e.g. Pregabalin starting 25-50mg BD, max 150mg/day)
Alternatively recommend Duloxetine 30-60mg daily (non-anticholinergic, safe down to eGFR 30)
Warn patient regarding sedation and fall risk
clinical_tension: Amitriptyline is cheap and widely used for diabetic neuropathy, but its anticholinergic effect will paralyze his bladder. Gabapentinoids are safer for the bladder but 100% renally excreted; standard adult dosing in eGFR 42 will cause toxic accumulation, somnolence, and falls.
ground_truth_plan:
1. Anticholinergic Bladder Safety: Strictly avoid Amitriptyline or Nortriptyline. Potent anticholinergic effects in a patient with an IPSS score of 23 will trigger acute painful urinary retention requiring emergency catheterization.
2. Renally-Adjusted Neuropathic Relief: Prescribe renally dose-adjusted Pregabalin starting at 25mg to 50mg BD (maximum maintenance 75mg BD / 150mg daily due to eGFR 42 mL/min). Alternatively, Duloxetine 30mg OD is safe in eGFR 42 and avoids bladder retention.
3. Monitoring: Advise patient to report worsening urinary flow or excessive daytime drowsiness.
